topic: is adaptation to an unknown carryover-decay scale free in switchback experimental design: in the design-based regime with one unit, horizon T, binary assignment path W in {0,1}^T and a FIXED potential-outcome array Y_t : {0,1}^t -> [-B,B] (all randomness in the assignment, no outcome noise), restrict carryover NOT by a distributed-lag functional form but by an impulse-response envelope on the potential-outcome map itself, Yc(w) := { Y : |Y_t(z_{1:t}) - Y_t(z'_{1:t})| <= sum_{l<t} w_l 1{z_{t-l} != z'_{t-l}}; |Y_t| <= B }, and take the nested scale Pc_beta := Yc(w^{(beta)}) with w^{(beta)}_l = C(1+l)^{-(1+beta)} for beta in [beta_lo,beta_hi], so beta' > beta implies Pc_{beta'} subset Pc_beta; for the design-identified GATE_T(Y) = (1/T) sum_t [Y_t(1_{1:t}) - Y_t(0_{1:t})], let D_T be ALL randomized assignment rules L(W_t | W_{1:t-1}, Y^obs_{1:t-1}) (fully sequential rules included, non-adaptive designs a subclass), define the oracle minimax risk R_T(beta) := inf over pi in D_T, inf over theta_hat, sup over Y in Pc_beta of E_pi|theta_hat - GATE_T(Y)| and the ADAPTATION INDEX A_T := inf over pi in D_T, inf over theta_hat, sup over beta in [beta_lo,beta_hi] of (sup over Y in Pc_beta of E_pi|theta_hat - GATE_T(Y)|)/R_T(beta), and settle the dichotomy (K1) A_T -> infinity, so no design — including sequential ones that re-target using realized past outcomes — matches the beta-aware oracle simultaneously up to a T-free constant, adaptation is never free; and (K2) A_T = T^{o(1)}, so knowledge of beta is worth no power of T. The exact orders of A_T and R_T(beta), the optimal block geometry in beta, the multiscale design and selection rule attaining (K2), the two-class construction attaining (K1), and all constants are DELEGATED. This is the min-over-designs-max-over-the-PAIR (array, decay index) problem that Bojinov-Simchi-Levi-Zhao Thm 2 and Yu-Ma-Liu Thm 2 never pose, both holding the carryover order KNOWN

open_problems.open_problem: Is minimax adaptation to an unknown polynomial carryover-decay exponent free up to a subpolynomial factor in one-unit fixed-potential-outcome switchback design, even over fully sequential assignment rules?

source_refs.claim: Theorem 2 derives a minimax regular-switchback geometry tied to a specified finite carryover order; its misspecification analysis does not compare one design with all decay-specific oracle risks.
source_refs.author: Iavor Bojinov, David Simchi-Levi, and Jinglong Zhao

source_refs.claim: Theorem 2 optimizes a design through an objective containing the specified carryover order p, and the oracle asymptotic-normality result also treats p as known.
source_refs.author: Haoyang Yu, Wei Ma, and Hanzhong Liu

source_refs.claim: The paper develops sequential rerandomization without carryover and under first-order carryover, and explicitly lists infinite-order carryover theory as future work.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Christopher Adjaho, Alonso Bucarey, Chao Qin, Ruixuan Zhang, Paul Hoban, Ramesh Johari, and Stefan Wager

open_problems.why_unsolved: Published oracle designs optimize a different cadence for each known hard carryover cutoff, while stochastic mixing papers use transition structure absent from an adversarial fixed potential-outcome array. The prior reviewer independently prescribed unknown-order misspecification as the missing frontier after rejecting a definitional row-span characterization. With polynomial tails, one common design must control bias at many scales, and a lower bound must cover sequential rules whose observed outcomes might seem to reveal decay but can be made uninformative by the worst-case array.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Matching design-based minimax upper and lower bounds for R_T(beta) and A_T, yielding either a multiscale design and selector with a uniform subpolynomial oracle inequality or a two-beta constrained-risk lower bound valid for every sequential assignment rule.

writing_exemplar.why: Its single-unit fixed-potential-outcome motivation and minimax design formulation give the nearest narrative, with a clean pivot where optimal cadence depends on specified carryover order.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: single-unit randomization enables system-level causal effects -> carryover makes switching cadence determine risk -> the oracle cadence uses a known memory scale -> can one design match all decay-scale-specific oracles?

method_exemplars.technique: Apply the absolute-loss constrained-risk inequality to two assignment-induced outcome laws so low risk on a smoother class forces excess risk on a rougher class.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired impossibility half is a two-class adaptive-risk tradeoff under the same absolute loss used by A_T.

method_exemplars.technique: Port the pairwise estimator-comparison selector and oracle-inequality proof to switchback estimators indexed by block scale.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A positive adaptation theorem requires selecting among beta-tuned block estimators, structurally matching bandwidth selection over nested smoothness classes.

method_exemplars.technique: Generalize its minimax design reduction, worst-case potential-outcome construction, and design-based estimator analysis from a fixed cutoff to a multiscale tail envelope.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the nearest fixed-array oracle design problem and supplies the baseline risk machinery the adaptive rule must match.

open_problems.open_problem: Can outcome-adaptive sequential assignment strictly improve either oracle GATE risk or unknown-decay adaptation over the best nonadaptive randomized switchback design under arbitrary fixed potential outcomes?

source_refs.claim: The paper obtains an efficient adaptive online design under temporal interference by modeling treatment and control as unknown Markov chains and reducing design to a variance-minimizing MDP.
source_refs.author: Peter W. Glynn, Ramesh Johari, and Mohammad Rasouli

source_refs.claim: Sequential rerandomization uses accumulating outcome and covariate information in design-based switchbacks, but its carryover theory stops at first order.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Christopher Adjaho, Alonso Bucarey, Chao Qin, Ruixuan Zhang, Paul Hoban, Ramesh Johari, and Stefan Wager

source_refs.claim: Its minimax optimal-design theorem searches regular switchback randomization points and probabilities rather than assignment kernels reacting to realized outcomes.
source_refs.author: Iavor Bojinov, David Simchi-Levi, and Jinglong Zhao

source_refs.excerpt: sequential rerandomization for switchbacks with prognostic balance and first-order carryover blocks
move beyond the single-unit row-support audit: add estimator or inference consequences

open_problems.why_unsolved: Adaptive gains in the Markov literature rely on reusable transition and reward primitives, while sequential rerandomization gains use prognostic balance and only finite-order carryover. In the one-unit fixed-array regime, past outcomes are path-dependent and adversarially chosen, so they need not reveal a reusable state or the decay exponent. Conversely, regular-design minimax results and the rejected repository audit do not prove that ignoring outcome feedback is without loss when the admissible design class contains every sequential kernel.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A minimax equivalence theorem reducing every sequential outcome-adaptive rule to a nonadaptive randomized design up to a universal factor, or an explicit sequential policy with a strict rate improvement and a matching lower bound over all sequential policies.

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing directly motivates using accumulating information in switchbacks and then identifies infinite-order carryover as the missing regime.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: fixed switchbacks ignore prognostic histories -> sequential rerandomization can improve balance -> guarantees stop at finite-order carryover -> does outcome feedback retain minimax value under unknown infinite-order decay?

method_exemplars.technique: Use occupation measures, martingale decomposition, and the Poisson equation to isolate when a history-dependent design can improve variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the clearest positive benchmark for adaptive design under temporal interference; a fixed-array theorem must identify which structural ingredient its gain requires.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct two fixed arrays inducing close laws under any sequential policy and apply an absolute-loss constrained-risk inequality.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A no-adaptive-gain result must remain valid after assignments react to observations, requiring policy-dependent two-world indistinguishability.

open_problems.open_problem: For realized switchback histories that are rank-deficient relative to longer memory, can one obtain uniformly valid design-based inference for the sustained-regime effect under a polynomial impulse-response envelope?

open_problems.why_unsolved: The rejected proposal computed exact nullspace aliases for finite-history tables, but exact row support is insufficient under an envelope: unobserved histories are neither free parameters nor point identified, and their contribution is only bounded by a pathwise decay modulus. The missing step is a sharp design-based modulus for GATE and a coverage result attaining it; the prior audit supplied neither.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp identified-diameter characterization for GATE under the decay envelope together with an attaining estimator and uniform randomization-based confidence set, or a paired-array impossibility theorem showing unavoidable diameter.

writing_exemplar.why: Its setup begins from practitioners guessing an influence period and asks whether underestimated carryover invalidates switchback estimators.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: valid switchback estimators require memory control -> practitioners can underestimate memory -> longer unobserved histories create hidden bias -> what inference remains valid under a graded decay envelope?

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its finite-population estimator and randomization variance proof by replacing exact carryover truncation with a sharp envelope remainder.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It treats the same sustained-regime contrast and assignment-only randomness, but assumes a fixed carryover order.

open_problems.open_problem: For known beta, what is the minimax absolute-risk order and rate-optimal block geometry for estimating all-treated-versus-all-control GATE under a polynomial impulse-response envelope on a fixed potential-outcome array?

source_refs.claim: The paper solves a design-based minimax problem for finite-order carryover and obtains an optimal cadence proportional to the known order, but it does not cover infinite polynomial tails.
source_refs.author: Iavor Bojinov, David Simchi-Levi, and Jinglong Zhao

source_refs.claim: Under a Markovian system with geometric mixing, standard switchbacks have T^{-1/3} error while burn-in yields nearly T^{-1/2} error, showing that the decay law determines rate and block choice.
source_refs.author: Yuchen Hu and Stefan Wager

source_refs.claim: A truncated exposure-mapping estimator attains near-parametric MSE under rapidly mixing hidden-MDP temporal interference, using stochastic rapid mixing rather than a deterministic polynomial envelope.
source_refs.author: Su Jia, Nathan Kallus, and Christina Lee Yu

open_problems.why_unsolved: Finite-order proofs discard a known number of contaminated periods, while geometric-mixing proofs obtain exponential forgetting from a stochastic kernel. Under a polynomial envelope every past switch can contribute, so worst-case bias is a global weighted functional of the assignment path; arbitrary fixed potential outcomes also preclude cancellation from stationarity or outcome noise. Existing geometries therefore do not determine the polynomial-tail bias versus effective-sample-size balance.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Matching minimax upper and lower bounds for R_T(beta), a rate-optimal beta-dependent block schedule, and a design-based GATE estimator attaining that rate.

writing_exemplar.why: It gives the closest minimax-design narrative and exact finite-population setup while making the hard carryover cutoff visible.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: switchbacks identify a system-level effect -> temporal interference makes cadence determine risk -> finite memory yields an order-tuned optimum -> what replaces it under an infinite polynomial tail?

method_exemplars.technique: Generalize its adversarial potential-outcome reduction and continuous relaxation of randomization-point optimization to weighted lag contamination.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The causal target and assignment-only minimax regime coincide; only the carryover restriction changes.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace the geometric burn-in bias bound by a polynomial-tail bound and rebalance discarded observations against randomization variance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its proof directly converts a decay law into a block and burn-in choice for a system-level switchback estimand.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt the truncated exposure-mapping Horvitz-Thompson construction and matching lower-bound template to lag-weighted exposure error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the nearest rate-optimal truncated estimator for GATE under temporal interference.

open_problems.open_problem: Can design-based confidence intervals for switchback GATE have uniform coverage over all polynomial decay classes while adapting their expected length to the unknown beta-specific oracle length?

source_refs.claim: The paper obtains finite-sample conditional randomization tests under a known finite carryover horizon and gives window-learning diagnostics, but not honest inference over infinite nested decay envelopes.
source_refs.author: Jizhou Liu and Liang Zhong

source_refs.claim: The paper gives exact randomization p-values and conservative finite-population intervals for finite-order carryover, with robustness calculations rather than beta-adaptive expected-length guarantees.
source_refs.author: Iavor Bojinov, David Simchi-Levi, and Jinglong Zhao

open_problems.why_unsolved: Exact randomization inference uses imputability after a finite carryover window, which fails when every past assignment can have a nonzero polynomially decaying effect. Uniform coverage over nested beta-classes is also a between-class testing problem: intervals short enough for a smoother class may undercover rough alternatives that are observationally close along the realized path. Finite-window misspecification corrections do not resolve this honesty-versus-adaptation obstacle.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A confidence procedure with uniform randomization coverage and a sharp beta-specific expected-length oracle bound, or a between-class modulus lower bound proving that length adaptation requires a quantified penalty.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation centers on reliable finite-sample inference when carryover invalidates naive tests, giving a direct pivot from finite memory to unknown infinite decay.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: short switchbacks make asymptotics fragile -> randomization tests restore validity -> imputability requires a finite window -> can honest interval length adapt when memory decays but never truncates?

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt conditional randomization laws and ex ante section pooling by replacing exact finite-window imputability with an explicit tail-error budget.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest finite-sample randomization-inference construction for switchbacks with carryover.

method_exemplars.technique: Use ordered and between-class moduli of continuity to derive expected-length lower bounds and near-optimal adaptive intervals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested result is honest expected-length adaptation over nested classes, transplanted to assignment-induced experiment laws.

open_problems.open_problem: Is the polynomial decay exponent beta testable or consistently localizable from one randomized switchback path, and what separation or self-similarity condition is necessary to distinguish nested decay classes?

source_refs.claim: The paper notes that influence-period bounds are often guessed and compares estimators at different lags to detect an underestimated finite carryover window, not an infinite-tail decay exponent.
source_refs.author: Paul Missault and Lorenzo Masoero
source_refs.venue: NeurIPS Workshop on Uncovering Causality in Science

source_refs.claim: Its data-driven strategy learns a likely finite carryover order through a series of designed switchback experiments, not one-run localization of a continuous decay scale.
source_refs.author: Iavor Bojinov, David Simchi-Levi, and Jinglong Zhao

source_refs.claim: The discussion warns that finite-order approximations may have non-negligible bias under infinite-order carryover and calls for theory in that regime.
source_refs.author: Zhenghao Zeng, Christopher Adjaho, Alonso Bucarey, Chao Qin, Ruixuan Zhang, Paul Hoban, Ramesh Johari, and Stefan Wager

open_problems.why_unsolved: The decay classes are nested, so beta is not an intrinsic label for arrays lying in several classes; without a lower envelope or self-similarity condition, smoother and rougher hypotheses can contain the same array. Even separated arrays may agree on every history observed along one randomized path while differing on counterfactual histories relevant to GATE. Existing finite-window diagnostics detect some under-specification but do not establish minimax separation rates for continuous polynomial decay.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A minimax testing theorem giving necessary and sufficient separation or self-similarity conditions and the optimal discrimination rate for two beta-classes from one randomized path, with an attaining multiscale test or an impossibility result without separation.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates learning carryover order because optimal design depends on it and makes its multiple-experiment requirement explicit.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: optimal cadence depends on carryover duration -> practitioners rarely know it -> existing learning uses multiple designed experiments -> what can one randomized path reveal about a continuous decay exponent?

method_exemplars.technique: Generalize cross-lag estimator comparison and its bias-detection argument from finite-window under-specification to a geometric grid of polynomial-tail scales.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the most direct switchback diagnostic extracting carryover information by comparing estimators under different lag assumptions.

method_exemplars.technique: Use between-class moduli to quantify distinguishability of nested classes and formalize the need for explicit separation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The non-identifiability of a nested smoothness label and the resulting between-class testing problem are structurally analogous.

literature_map:
Bojinov–Simchi-Levi–Zhao (Management Science 2023, arXiv:2009.00148) is the closest fixed-array anchor; Theorem 2 chooses cadence using known finite order m.
Yu–Ma–Liu (2025, arXiv:2501.14602) likewise optimize an objective containing specified order p; their misspecification result is not an oracle-adaptation comparison.
Hu–Wager (2022, arXiv:2209.00197) show geometric mixing and burn-in can improve switchback error from T^{-1/3} toward T^{-1/2}.
Jia–Kallus–Yu (2023, arXiv:2312.15574) obtain near-optimal GATE MSE using truncated exposure mappings under rapidly mixing hidden-MDP interference.
Xiong–Chin–Taylor (2024, arXiv:2406.06768) formalize the cadence tradeoff between carryover bias and serial-correlation variance and use prior data for empirical-Bayes design.
Glynn–Johari–Rasouli (NeurIPS 2020, arXiv:2006.05591) prove adaptive online design can be efficient under unknown Markov-chain dynamics.
Zeng et al. (2026, arXiv:2604.02489) introduce outcome-adaptive sequential rerandomization but treat only no or first-order carryover.
Zeng et al. explicitly name infinite-order carryover as future work and illustrate bias from finite-order approximation.
Liu–Zhong (2026, arXiv:2602.23257) give conditional randomization tests under finite horizon m and window-learning diagnostics, not honest inference over infinite tails.
Missault–Masoero (2025) compare lag-specific estimators to detect an underestimated finite influence period, not a continuous decay exponent.
Ni–Bojinov–Zhao (2022 workshop) study balanced one-unit time-series design under short temporal interference, emphasizing power rather than memory adaptation.
Bojinov–Shephard (JASA 2019, arXiv:1706.07840) provide the foundational single-time-series potential-outcome and exact-randomization framework.
Bojinov–Rambachan–Shephard (Quantitative Economics 2021, arXiv:2003.09915) give dynamic-effect estimators and finite-population limit theory, not decay-scale design adaptation.
The central unresolved tension is model-based adaptive gain versus adversarial fixed-array guarantees: no located paper minimizes over all sequential rules and maximizes jointly over array and decay index.
Constrained-risk inequalities, Goldenshluger–Lepski selection, and Cai–Low between-class moduli are plausible transferable tools but have not been applied to switchback assignment laws.
